messages:
sec-bot: ALERT: Config scanner detected ingress 0.0.0.0/0 on security-group `inference-gpu-sg` for ports 22 and 6379 in acct redwood-prod us-west-2 :exclamation:
alia: seeing it, grabbing context. which TF PR changed this? :eyes:
matt: PR #4623 (infra/inference) merged ~15m ago. author @jordan.
jordan: yep that was me, trying to add a jump host rule quickly and must've copy/pasted. sorry — pushing fix now.
alia: ok. containment plan: (1) remove wide ingress (2) restrict to office and VPC CIDRs (3) rotate Redis AUTH token and check any RDB snapshots uploaded to S3 for public access (4) preserve logs for audit. agree?
samir: +1. also turn on VPC Flow log snippet for the subnet and export to secure bucket for 30d. check CloudTrail for AssumeRole or unusual API calls around the hosts.
kevin: if any snapshot encryption uses CMK, verify key policy — don't rotate before confirming snapshot access. we need to know whether RDB snapshots were ever exported externally.
opsbot: running emergency change: terraform apply -target=aws_security_group_rule.inference_restricting_rule --auto-approve (plan id: p-7a9)
opsbot: apply complete. removed 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on ports 22 and 6379; added allow from 10.0.0.0/8 and office IP list.
alia: good. @jordan please open a revert PR for the original change and include test/plan output.
jordan: opened PR #4624 with revert + stricter rule. gist:```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "inference_allow_internal" {
  type        = "ingress"
  from_port   = 6379
  to_port     = 6379
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/8", "203.0.113.5/32"]
}
```
alia: on Redis auth rotation: run `aws elasticache modify-replication-group --replication-group-id inference-redis --auth-token <new>` with ApplyImmediately true. coordinate with app team for small window.
matt: app team on standby. doing token rotate now.
opsbot: rotation invoked, status: modifying. note: client libs will reconnect.
samir: while that's running: search S3 for any public RDB snapshots. command: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-backups --prefix rdb/inference/ --query "Contents[?contains(Key, 'rdb')]|[0].Key"`
kevin: found two snapshots from last week: rdb/inference/inference-2026-03-10.rdb — checking ACLs...
kevin: bucket redwood-backups policy shows `BlockPublicAcls` = false for that lifecycle. setting BlockPublicAcls=true and removing public-read ACLs now.
alia: good. also check if any presigned URLs were generated. audit CloudTrail for `CreatePresignedUrl` and S3:PutObjectAcl.
samir: CloudTrail lookup: no PutObjectAcl from external principals, presigned URL creation calls are application-side and look normal. no cross-account AssumeRole during window.
matt: Redis rotate completed, clients reconnected.
jordan: quick scan of hosts in the SG: no suspicious processes; verified last successful SSHs were by our bastion IPs only.
kevin: snapshot ACLs cleaned, bucket policy tightened, Object Lock not needed. KMS: snapshots encrypted with customer-managed key `alias/redwood-rdb-cmk` — key policy OK, no external principals.
alia: excellent. next steps (post-incident):
- create a hard deny guardrail in org-terraform to block 0.0.0.0/0 for infra SGs (pre-commit check + policy as code).
- add a required review by security for any SG changes touching inference or prod tags.
- enable terraform plan scanning in CI for new rules.
- add an alert to sec-bot for any future wide ingress on sensitive ports.
- include this incident in next internal all-hands and run a 15-min blameless recap.
matt: I’ll own the pre-commit rule and the PR template change. ETA EOD.
jordan: I’ll do the revert + add test to cover the jump host change.
kevin: I’ll verify snapshots & KMS safe handling, add S3 BlockPublicPolicy enforcement in bucket lifecycle.
samir: I’ll draft the brief incident note and link logs + timelines. we should also add an automation: when a tf plan would add 0.0.0.0/0, fail the run and notify PR author.
alia: agree. any evidence of exfil or external access?
kevin: no signs. VPC Flow logs show only short-lived connection attempts from random IPs during the window but no large transfers, CloudTrail shows no data-access API calls from unusual principals.
alia: marking this as contained. create incident ticket in opsgenie and assign follow-ups.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0347. owner @matt. priority P2. link: https://redwood.opsgenie.io/incident/INC-2026-0347
matt: copying notes into the ticket. thanks all, lesson learned. :lock: 
kevin: adding a follow-up to rotate any long-lived keys that could've touched those hosts, just in case.
samir: scheduled blameless postmortem for tomorrow 09:30 PT. invite prod infra, sec, and app owners.
alia: closing thread here — if you see new anomalies ping #eng-oncall and @sec-bot. :thumbsup:
